cards.explanation: The answer is that David tells his soul not to forget all His kind deeds. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), says, "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds…" (Psalm 103:2). I once searched the whole bakery for my chef's hat while it was sitting on my head. If a stamper can lose track of what's right on top of him, a soul can lose track of kind deeds. So David keeps them in front of his soul.

The word is forgives, friends. David says it's He "…who forgives all your iniquities and heals all your diseases…" (Psalm 103:3). Look at that word ALL. It shows up twice in one verse, and David doesn't leave anything out. When David lists kind deeds for his soul, forgiveness is first on the list.

The answer is loving devotion and compassion, bakers. The LORD "…redeems your life from the Pit and crowns you with loving devotion and compassion…" (Psalm 103:4). Think about that. A crown is usually made of metal, and this one is made of devotion and compassion. I'd take that over any hat, and I own a tall white one.

The answer is that it is renewed like the eagle's. The LORD "…satisfies you with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s." (Psalm 103:5). David picks an eagle for his picture. Renewed means made fresh again, and I know a little about that, since I went from a junk drawer to a bakery.

The answer is all the oppressed, friends. "The LORD executes righteousness and justice for all the oppressed." (Psalm 103:6). David has been talking to his own soul. Now he looks at people who are being pushed down. The ones who need justice are the ones the verse names.

The answer is True, bakers. David says, "He made known His ways to Moses, His deeds to the people of Israel." (Psalm 103:7). So the LORD made His ways known to Moses, Israel's leader. And He made His deeds known to the people of Israel.

The answer is slow to anger, friends. David says, "The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion." (Psalm 103:8). Compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in loving devotion. That's four things in one verse. I'd take any one of them.

The answer is False, bakers. David says, "He has not dealt with us according to our sins or repaid us according to our iniquities." (Psalm 103:10). Our sins don't set the terms for how the LORD treats us. That fits what David just said in verse 8, that the LORD is "…slow to anger…"

The answer is those who fear Him, friends. David says, "For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His loving devotion for those who fear Him." (Psalm 103:11). David compares how great His loving devotion is to how high the heavens are above the earth. And it's for those who fear Him.

The answer is our transgressions, bakers. "As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us." (Psalm 103:12). Think about it. If you go east you keep going east, and you never hit west. That's a lot of distance, and David says it's how far our transgressions have been removed.

The word is father, friends. David says, "As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him." (Psalm 103:13). That's a dad looking after his children. I have six little cookie cutter kids, so this one lands close to home.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "For He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust." (Psalm 103:14). The LORD isn't surprised by how small and fragile we are. He knows it, and He keeps it in mind. That comes right after David says the LORD has compassion like a father.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "…when the wind passes over, it vanishes, and its place remembers it no more." (Psalm 103:16). So there's no growing back stronger in that picture. David is showing how brief our days are, and the next verse gives the contrast.

The answer is from everlasting to everlasting, bakers. David says, "But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him…" (Psalm 103:17). Notice that little word BUT. The flower vanishes when the wind passes over it (Psalm 103:16), and the LORD's loving devotion doesn't end. That's good news.

The answer is True, friends. David says the LORD's loving devotion extends to those who fear Him, "…and His righteousness to their children’s children…" (Psalm 103:17). So it reaches past one lifetime and on to the next generations. That's a long way to carry something.

The word is all, bakers. David says, "The LORD has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all." (Psalm 103:19). Nothing is left off that list. David is praising the LORD while looking at something much bigger than himself.

The answer is His angels, friends. David says, "Bless the LORD, all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word, who hearken to the voice of His command." (Psalm 103:20). They're mighty in strength, and they carry out His word. If those heavy hitters are called to bless the LORD, then I'm happy to join in.
